title: Laboratory Automation & ICT
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Science Laboratory Technology 300L curriculum: computer and ICT fundamentals as applied to the modern laboratory -- LIMS, data acquisition, instrument interfacing, automation/control concepts, data integrity, and common lab software tools.

questions.question: What does LIMS stand for in a modern analytical laboratory?
options: Laboratory Instrument Management Software
Laboratory Information Management System
Local Instrument Monitoring Service
Linked Inventory Management Server
questions.correct_answer: Laboratory Information Management System
questions.explanation: LIMS (Laboratory Information Management System) is software that tracks samples, test results, and workflow data through the laboratory's testing process.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using a LIMS to track samples from receipt to final report?
options: It eliminates the need for any quality control
It provides traceability, reduces transcription errors, and links each result to its sample and instrument
It automatically performs all chemical analyses without an analyst
It replaces the need for sample labelling
questions.correct_answer: It provides traceability, reduces transcription errors, and links each result to its sample and instrument
questions.explanation: A LIMS creates an auditable chain linking sample, method, instrument, analyst and result, cutting manual transcription errors compared with paper logs.

questions.question: The data integrity principle 'ALCOA' requires that laboratory records be:
options: Attractive, Legible, Correct, Official, Accurate
Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate
Automated, Linked, Compressed, Organized, Archived
Anonymous, Locked, Copied, Ordered, Approved
questions.correct_answer: Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate
questions.explanation: ALCOA is the standard data-integrity acronym: records must be Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, and Accurate.

questions.question: In signal terms, a thermocouple's raw voltage output before digitization is best described as:
options: A digital signal
An analog signal
A binary signal
A network packet
questions.correct_answer: An analog signal
questions.explanation: A thermocouple produces a continuously varying voltage proportional to temperature, which is an analog signal until it is converted to discrete digital values.

questions.question: What is the function of an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) in a computer-interfaced instrument?
options: It converts digital data into a printed report
It converts a continuous analog sensor signal into discrete digital values a computer can process
It amplifies the mains power supply
It converts digital signals back into analog only
questions.correct_answer: It converts a continuous analog sensor signal into discrete digital values a computer can process
questions.explanation: An ADC samples a continuous analog signal (e.g. from a sensor) and converts it into discrete numeric values that a computer's data acquisition software can store and process.

questions.question: A data acquisition system (DAQ) attached to a laboratory instrument primarily serves to:
options: Manually record readings into a logbook
Automatically capture, digitize, and store measurement data from sensors in real time
Replace the need for any sensor
Sterilize the instrument between runs
questions.correct_answer: Automatically capture, digitize, and store measurement data from sensors in real time
questions.explanation: A DAQ system continuously samples sensor outputs, converts them to digital form, and logs the data, removing the need for manual reading and recording.

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical device that detects a change in a physical quantity (e.g. temperature, pressure) and converts it into a measurable signal?
options: A transducer/sensor
A compiler
A router
A spreadsheet macro
questions.correct_answer: A transducer/sensor
questions.explanation: A transducer (sensor) converts a physical quantity such as temperature, pressure or pH into an electrical signal that can be measured or recorded.

questions.question: In an automated titrator, what does the term 'endpoint detection' typically rely on?
options: A human visually watching the color change every time
A potentiometric or optical sensor that detects the equivalence point electronically
Manual stopwatch timing only
The barcode printed on the sample bottle
questions.correct_answer: A potentiometric or optical sensor that detects the equivalence point electronically
questions.explanation: Automated titrators use a pH/potentiometric or photometric sensor to detect the inflection point of the titration curve, removing the need for a human to watch a color-change indicator.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of an autosampler on an HPLC or GC instrument?
options: It eliminates the need for a mobile phase
It allows unattended, sequential injection of many samples with consistent, reproducible injection volumes
It automatically writes the final analytical report
It replaces the detector
questions.correct_answer: It allows unattended, sequential injection of many samples with consistent, reproducible injection volumes
questions.explanation: Autosamplers inject a queue of samples automatically and reproducibly, improving throughput and reducing the injection-volume variability of manual injection.

questions.question: A Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) used in an automated laboratory or process line is best described as:
options: A device dedicated only to printing labels
An industrial digital computer that executes control logic to operate equipment based on sensor inputs
A type of analytical balance
A category of glassware
questions.correct_answer: An industrial digital computer that executes control logic to operate equipment based on sensor inputs
questions.explanation: A PLC is a ruggedized industrial computer programmed with control logic (e.g. ladder logic) to automate equipment operation based on real-time sensor input.

questions.question: In a closed-loop (feedback) control system, what happens after the sensor detects a deviation from the setpoint?
options: Nothing; the system runs open-ended with no correction
The controller compares it to the setpoint and adjusts the actuator to correct the deviation
The setpoint is deleted
The sensor is disconnected automatically
questions.correct_answer: The controller compares it to the setpoint and adjusts the actuator to correct the deviation
questions.explanation: Closed-loop control continuously compares measured output to a desired setpoint via the controller and drives an actuator to minimize the error, e.g. an incubator maintaining set temperature.

questions.question: How does an open-loop control system differ from a closed-loop system?
options: An open-loop system has no feedback path and does not adjust its output based on measured results
An open-loop system is always more accurate
There is no practical difference
Open-loop systems cannot be automated
questions.correct_answer: An open-loop system has no feedback path and does not adjust its output based on measured results
questions.explanation: Open-loop control applies a preset action without measuring or correcting for the actual output, unlike closed-loop control which continuously corrects based on feedback.

questions.question: Which file format is most commonly used to export tabular laboratory data for exchange between different software programs?
options: CSV (comma-separated values)
MP3
JPEG
EXE
questions.correct_answer: CSV (comma-separated values)
questions.explanation: CSV is a plain-text tabular format widely supported by spreadsheet, database, and statistical software for straightforward data exchange.

questions.question: Which type of software would a technologist use to organize calibration curve data, calculate a regression line, and plot results?
options: A spreadsheet program such as Microsoft Excel
A video editing program
An operating system kernel
An email client
questions.correct_answer: A spreadsheet program such as Microsoft Excel
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet software provides formulas, linear regression and charting tools well suited to building and plotting calibration curves from instrument response data.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a spreadsheet and a relational database for storing laboratory data?
options: There is no difference at all
A database enforces structured relationships and referential integrity across tables, while a spreadsheet is a flat grid of cells
Spreadsheets can never store numbers
Databases cannot store text data
questions.correct_answer: A database enforces structured relationships and referential integrity across tables, while a spreadsheet is a flat grid of cells
questions.explanation: Relational databases link related tables (e.g. samples, tests, results) with defined relationships and constraints, offering more structure and integrity than a flat spreadsheet.

questions.question: An Electronic Laboratory Notebook (ELN) improves on a traditional paper notebook mainly by:
options: Being impossible to back up
Providing searchable, time-stamped, auditable digital records that can be linked to instrument data
Removing the need for any experimental record at all
Allowing entries to be freely altered with no trace
questions.correct_answer: Providing searchable, time-stamped, auditable digital records that can be linked to instrument data
questions.explanation: ELNs give time-stamped, version-controlled, searchable digital entries with audit trails, improving traceability over handwritten paper notebooks.

questions.question: Which computer hardware component is often called the 'brain' of the computer, executing instructions?
options: Central Processing Unit (CPU)
Monitor
Mouse
USB flash drive
questions.correct_answer: Central Processing Unit (CPU)
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches, decodes, and executes instructions, coordinating the operations of all other computer hardware components.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an input device on a laboratory computer workstation?
options: A keyboard
A printer
A monitor
A speaker
questions.correct_answer: A keyboard
questions.explanation: A keyboard sends data into the computer, making it an input device, whereas monitors, printers and speakers are output devices.

questions.question: What is the main function of an operating system (e.g. Windows) on a laboratory computer?
options: It performs chemical analysis directly
It manages hardware resources and provides a platform on which application software (e.g. instrument control software) runs
It is a type of laboratory glassware
It generates electrical power for instruments
questions.correct_answer: It manages hardware resources and provides a platform on which application software (e.g. instrument control software) runs
questions.explanation: An operating system manages memory, storage, and peripherals, and provides the environment in which instrument-control and data-analysis software run.

questions.question: A barcode or RFID tag attached to a sample container is primarily used to:
options: Sterilize the sample
Uniquely identify and track the sample through the laboratory workflow via a LIMS
Change the sample's pH
Replace the need for a sample label entirely with no identifying data
questions.correct_answer: Uniquely identify and track the sample through the laboratory workflow via a LIMS
questions.explanation: Barcodes and RFID tags carry a unique sample ID that a LIMS can scan to track chain-of-custody, location, and status automatically, reducing manual logging errors.

questions.question: Why is a scheduled, verified data backup important for a laboratory's electronic records?
options: It is not important since paper copies are always kept instead
It protects against data loss from hardware failure, corruption, or accidental deletion
It slows the computer down for no benefit
It is required only for image files
questions.correct_answer: It protects against data loss from hardware failure, corruption, or accidental deletion
questions.explanation: Regular verified backups ensure that critical test results and records can be recovered if original files are lost to hardware failure, corruption, or human error.

questions.question: What is a Local Area Network (LAN) in the context of a laboratory's ICT infrastructure?
options: A network confined to a limited area, such as one building, connecting lab computers and instruments together
A single standalone computer with no connections
An instrument that only works when powered off
A type of glassware calibration standard
questions.correct_answer: A network confined to a limited area, such as one building, connecting lab computers and instruments together
questions.explanation: A LAN connects computers, servers, and networked instruments within a limited geographic area (e.g. one lab or building) so data and resources can be shared.

questions.question: Why is basic cybersecurity (e.g. strong passwords, restricted user access) important for a LIMS or lab computer network?
options: It has no relevance to laboratory work
It protects patient/client confidentiality and prevents unauthorized alteration or loss of test data
It is required only for social media accounts
It replaces the need for calibration
questions.correct_answer: It protects patient/client confidentiality and prevents unauthorized alteration or loss of test data
questions.explanation: Restricting access and using strong authentication protects sensitive results from unauthorized viewing, tampering, or deletion, preserving data confidentiality and integrity.

questions.question: Which interface/port type has historically been used to connect older laboratory instruments to a computer for data transfer, alongside modern USB connections?
options: RS-232 (serial) port
HDMI audio jack
SIM card slot
Ethernet power socket
questions.correct_answer: RS-232 (serial) port
questions.explanation: RS-232 is a long-standing serial communication standard widely used to interface older analytical instruments (e.g. balances, pH meters) with computers.

questions.question: Before relying on a new software update to control a critical laboratory instrument, what should be done first?
options: Install it directly onto the only working instrument with no testing
Validate/verify the software update in a controlled way to confirm it performs as expected before routine use
Delete all previous calibration records
Skip any testing since software updates are always safe
questions.correct_answer: Validate/verify the software update in a controlled way to confirm it performs as expected before routine use
questions.explanation: Software that controls or processes critical laboratory data should be validated/verified after any update to confirm correct, reliable performance before it is used for routine reporting.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) connected to a laboratory computer or instrument?
options: To increase the instrument's analytical sensitivity
To provide short-term backup power and protect against data loss during a power outage or surge
To calibrate the instrument automatically
To replace the need for an operating system
questions.correct_answer: To provide short-term backup power and protect against data loss during a power outage or surge
questions.explanation: A UPS bridges brief power interruptions and buffers against surges, giving time to save data or shut down safely and protecting sensitive electronics from power fluctuation damage.

questions.question: In statistical software (e.g. SPSS, Minitab) used to analyze replicate laboratory results, which function is most directly useful for comparing the means of two independent sample groups?
options: An independent-samples t-test
A spell-check function
A font formatting tool
An image compression tool
questions.correct_answer: An independent-samples t-test
questions.explanation: An independent-samples t-test statistically compares the means of two unrelated groups, a common task when comparing analytical results between two methods or conditions.

questions.question: Why do laboratories increasingly use automated liquid-handling robots for sample preparation in high-throughput testing?
options: Robots cannot pipette accurately
They increase throughput and reduce pipetting variability and operator fatigue compared to manual repetitive pipetting
They eliminate the need for any quality control checks
They are required only for qualitative tests
questions.correct_answer: They increase throughput and reduce pipetting variability and operator fatigue compared to manual repetitive pipetting
questions.explanation: Automated liquid handlers perform repetitive pipetting with high reproducibility and speed, reducing human error and fatigue in high-volume sample preparation.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of version/document control (e.g. numbered SOP revisions) in a laboratory's ICT/document system?
options: To make old documents impossible to retrieve
To ensure only the current, approved version of a procedure is in active use and superseded versions are withdrawn
To increase the file size of documents
To prevent any document from ever being updated
questions.correct_answer: To ensure only the current, approved version of a procedure is in active use and superseded versions are withdrawn
questions.explanation: Version control ensures every user references the current, approved procedure, preventing outdated or superseded methods from being followed in error.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of read-only or restricted-permission settings applied to finalized instrument result files?
options: To prevent the file from ever being viewed again
To prevent unauthorized editing of results after they have been recorded, preserving data integrity
To make the file load faster
To automatically delete the file after 24 hours
questions.correct_answer: To prevent unauthorized editing of results after they have been recorded, preserving data integrity
questions.explanation: Locking finalized result files against editing protects the original recorded data from accidental or deliberate alteration, a core data-integrity control.

questions.question: A technologist wants to automatically flag any result that falls outside a defined acceptable range in a spreadsheet. Which spreadsheet feature is best suited for this?
options: Conditional formatting combined with an IF function
Changing the file extension
Printing the spreadsheet on colored paper
Increasing the font size
questions.correct_answer: Conditional formatting combined with an IF function
questions.explanation: Conditional formatting paired with a logical IF function can automatically highlight or flag cells whose values fall outside specified control limits.

questions.question: In computer terminology, RAM (Random Access Memory) is best described as:
options: Permanent storage that keeps data after the computer is switched off
Fast, temporary working memory the CPU uses to run active programs and data
A type of printer
A network cable
questions.correct_answer: Fast, temporary working memory the CPU uses to run active programs and data
questions.explanation: RAM temporarily holds data and instructions that the CPU is actively using; its contents are lost when power is removed, unlike permanent storage such as a hard drive.
